# Smartest

Smartest is a small Ruby test runner that brings Pytest-style fixtures for Ruby:
keyword-argument fixture injection, explicit fixture dependencies, fixture
cleanup, and a focused CLI runner.

Use this page as an LLM-friendly entry point. For canonical human-readable
documentation, prefer the project README and the public docs linked below.

## Canonical Links

- README: https://github.com/YusukeIwaki/smartest#readme
- Documentation home: https://smartest-rb.vercel.app/docs/intro
- Getting started: https://smartest-rb.vercel.app/docs/getting-started
- Fixtures: https://smartest-rb.vercel.app/docs/fixtures
- Stubs: https://smartest-rb.vercel.app/docs/stubs
- Running test suites: https://smartest-rb.vercel.app/docs/running-test-suites
- Matchers: https://smartest-rb.vercel.app/docs/matchers
- Playwright browser tests: https://smartest-rb.vercel.app/docs/playwright-browser-tests

## Core Concepts

- Tests are declared with the top-level `test` method.
- Assertions use `expect(actual).to matcher`, `expect(actual).not_to matcher`,
  and block expectations such as `expect { action }.to raise_error(...)`.
- Fixture classes inherit from `Smartest::Fixture`.
- `fixture :name` defines a test-scoped fixture.
- `suite_fixture :name` defines a lazy suite-scoped fixture shared across the
  full suite.
- Tests and fixtures request dependencies with required Ruby keyword arguments.
- `use_fixture` registers fixture classes from `around_suite` or `around_test`.
- `cleanup` registers teardown for resources owned by a fixture. Test-scoped
  fixture cleanup runs after the test; suite fixture cleanup runs after the
  suite.
- `simple_stub_any_instance_of(Klass, :method) { ... }` and
  `simple_stub(object, :method) { ... }` are fixture helpers that apply a
  Fiber-local stub and register cleanup automatically.
- `Smartest::SimpleStub.new(Klass, :method) { ... }` is the low-level API for
  manually applying and resetting a Fiber-local stub.
- Fixture values are cached within one test. Regular fixtures get a fresh cache
  for each test.
- Duplicate fixture names across registered fixture classes and circular fixture
  dependencies are reported as errors.
- The CLI runs `smartest/**/*_test.rb` by default and also accepts explicit file,
  glob, line, and line-range arguments.

## Example

```ruby
class WebFixture < Smartest::Fixture
  fixture :server do
    server = TestServer.start
    cleanup { server.stop }
    server
  end

  fixture :client do |server:|
    Client.new(base_url: server.url)
  end
end

around_suite do |suite|
  use_fixture WebFixture
  suite.run
end

test("GET /health") do |client:|
  response = client.get("/health")

  expect(response.status).to eq(200)
end
```

## Current Scope

Smartest currently focuses on a small runner API: `test`, `expect`, fixtures,
suite fixtures, fixture cleanup, `around_suite`, `around_test`, `skip`,
`pending`, helper and matcher registration, console reporting, and the CLI
runner.

Nested `describe` blocks, watch mode, parallel execution, and file-scoped
fixtures are not part of the current MVP.
